# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 2, 2026

S2 Make TinyDB JSONStorage writes crash-safe so a process dying mid-write cannot leave a truncated db.json (Nov 2, 8:16 PM)

5 " ✓ Uncommitted crash-safe JSONStorage edits reverted; working tree restored to index
6 8:20p ◆ JSONStorage.write now saves via temp file, fsync, and atomic rename
7 " ◆ Added crash-safety and round-trip tests for JSONStorage writes
8 " ○ Test run fails because pytest.ini passes coverage options that pytest rejects
9 " ○ Full tinydb suite passes with 232 tests when pytest.ini is bypassed
S3 Make TinyDB JSONStorage writes crash-safe after an OOM kill truncated db.json, so that a process dying mid-write leaves a readable database on next open, with tests added. (Nov 2, 8:20 PM)
**Investigated**: tinydb/storages.py was read and the original JSONStorage.write path was traced. The original write seeks to 0, writes in place through a persistent handle, flushes, fsyncs, and only then truncates. The test directory was listed and git status was checked. The full suite was run, first with pytest.ini, which failed on unrecognized --cov arguments, and then with -c /dev/null.

**Completed**: JSONStorage.write in tinydb/storages.py was reimplemented to serialize first, write to a same-directory temp file, fsync it, and os.replace it over the target, then fsync the directory. The target path is resolved through realpath so symlinks are preserved, and file permission bits are copied. The write handle is reopened after each write. Writes in a read-only access mode still raise IOError. Four tests were appended to tests/test_storages.py: interrupted write keeps old data with no temp leftovers, serialization error keeps old data, write and reopen round-trip, and symlink and mode preservation. The suite passes 232 tests. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: The work is at a checkpoint. Nothing is actively in progress from the observed output. The most likely next items are verifying the single-file bind-mount constraint mentioned in the agent's response and deciding whether to commit the change.

**Notes**: The agent's response claims a single-file bind mount breaks os.replace and a session note mentions this constraint. No tool output in the observed window confirmed either point, so treat the claim as unverified. The response also attributes the truncation to the OOM kill, and that link is not confirmed by tool output either. This change fixes only JSONStorage writes and does not address the OOM kill itself. The pytest.ini coverage dependency remains unresolved for the default test invocation.
